notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed (authored_by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, reviewed_by null): the loader refuses this R2 hardware backend until a human signs reviewed_by, and nothing ran on a robot. The hardware backend also needs unitree_sdk2py, which pyproject.toml:21 leaves commented out, plus a live DDS domain and an rt/lowstate publisher; none of that was installed or run here. Nothing in the pinned clone was modified, imported or run during this work (git status clean at 41c2805742de879ddab2d8d6beaeaf215f876395).

DEVICE AND DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's family is python-object/PythonObjectDriver, but the chosen entry is the default G1_29_ArmController (utils.py:125, make_robot.py:94). Its state and target are 14-element arrays and its only control is ctrl_dual_arm(q_target, tauff_target); a direct decorated Driver expresses that array interface and the hold stop more directly than the config-only PythonObjectDriver maps. The card's candidate classes (sensing.read, device.configure, device.calibrate) do not bind joint motion; the catalogue class cap.motion.joint_position.v1 (resource kind robot.arm) binds the primary control. NOT COVERED: the feedforward torque half of ctrl_dual_arm is sent as zero, because the catalogue joint-position class has no torque field and the clone states no torque bound; deployment torque feedforward is not covered and needs an operator-defined extension if required.

MOCK PATH: the card's mock_strategy hints are IsaacSim camera/state topics; there is no upstream simulator or recorded traffic for G1_29_ArmController. The package fake (fake.py) is an analytic in-memory stand-in, not a recording: it has no DDS, no 250 Hz publish thread, no velocity clip and no motion over time; a stored target is copied to the current q when the call returns. It does not prove the stop or any motion. The real constructor blocks until the first rt/lowstate message and has no timeout; that deployment wait is outside the fake.

LIMITS: the clone states no G1 arm joint travel range, so joint_positions is Limit.operator_required. Without an operator site-limits.json every move is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. site-limits.example.json contains example-only placeholder +/-1.0 rad values for the example bench; they are not real joint limits and must not be used as such.

STOP: the class has no stop, disable, brake or emergency method; ctrl_dual_arm_go_home is a home move, not a stop. The @estop and the safe-state action x-cap.unitreerobotics.hold_position.v1 use the last q from the subscribed LowState buffer and send it back through ctrl_dual_arm with zero feedforward torque. The daemon publisher keeps publishing the hold, so the stop is not a sensed quiescence and the driver does not claim one. The publish loop copies the target under ctrl_lock and writes it outside the lock, so one more LowCmd with the previous target may be published before it reads the hold target. The LowState buffer has no freshness check: if the DDS stream stopped, the hold target is the last received q and may be stale. The clone documents no physical e-stop; the deployment must provide an independent hardware stop, and this hold is not a safety-rated stop. There is no @reset hook and no reenable action: a reset only releases the latch, and the next move command is a normal motion target.

No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings and no other gate warnings. Only the safe-state extension id is used; it is listed in catalogue_requests. The gate digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-17; reviewed_by stays null): Blocked because ctrl_dual_arm only stores targets from an undated LowState buffer and confirms no physical stop while the daemon publisher keeps running. Changed driver.py to fail every best-effort e-stop with the latch held and make hold_position an ordinary action; fake.py now stores targets without changing measured positions. Corrected constructor, publisher-loop and hard-coded speed-ramp citations in driver.py and facts.md, then regenerated reference.json and REFERENCE.md. Updated test_driver.py with honest failure/latch assertions; all 10 additional cases pass and the stock gate assertion remains unchanged. check-report.json fails G3 SAFE-045 after removal of the unsupported safe-state action; strict collection reports RESULT_UNTRUSTED until the orchestrator applies the block to the unchanged author RESULT.json. For the human reviewer: Unblocking needs a source-backed acknowledged stop and a valid R2 independent-stop/safe-state declaration. Construction joins DDS domain 0 by default, waits indefinitely for LowState, enables motor modes/PD gains for non-arm joints too, and starts the arm publisher with zero q_target; a publisher iteration may already hold an older target when the hold request arrives. Dex3_1_Controller and the serial UnitreeMotorSDK are separate card entries and are not served. The unitree_sdk2py dependency remains external and commented out upstream; no hardware was run.

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class models an input-free hold of the last joint positions that can serve as the safe-state action at R2. cap.motion.joint_position.v1 requires joint_positions, and the stop classes stop a device rather than hold this controller. The upstream class has no stop, disable or emergency method, so the only available safe action is the last q from the subscribed LowState buffer sent back through ctrl_dual_arm with zero feedforward torque. The extension takes no input and returns whether the hold target was sent.
catalogue_requests.summary: Hold the last fourteen arm joint positions from the LowState buffer with zero feedforward torque as the safe-state action.
